drills.q: State the agent loop and name three valid stop conditions.
drills.a: Observe -> reason -> act -> observe, repeat. Stop conditions: max-iteration cap, model-emitted 'done' signal, cost/token budget ceiling -- need at least two simultaneously.

drills.q: Give the Reciprocal Rank Fusion formula for hybrid search and why naive score averaging is a bug.
drills.a: score = sum over ranked lists of 1/(k+rank_i), k~60. Naive averaging is a bug because raw BM25 scores and cosine similarity scales aren't comparable -- you'd be averaging incommensurable numbers.

drills.q: Retrieval recall looks fine but answer quality is bad. How do you tell if it's a chunking problem?
drills.a: Inspect the actual retrieved chunk text for the failing queries -- check whether the answer was split across a chunk boundary such that the model only saw half of it, rather than assuming the generation step is at fault.

drills.q: Why can't you just use a cross-encoder for the whole corpus and skip bi-encoder retrieval?
drills.a: There's nothing to precompute for a cross-encoder -- the score depends jointly on the query, unknown until query time. A full transformer forward pass per (query, document) across a million-row corpus is computationally infeasible at any real-time latency budget.

drills.q: An LLM-judge says groundedness is 95% but users report made-up answers weekly. First hypothesis?
drills.a: The judge model may be systematically miscalibrated on a specific failure category (e.g. numeric hallucinations, hard for another LLM to catch without doing the arithmetic itself) -- stratify the eval by failure category rather than trust the aggregate number.

drills.q: When is long context actually the right call over RAG?
drills.a: When the task requires reasoning across the ENTIRE document coherently (e.g. summarizing overall contract risk) rather than retrieving discrete facts, or when the corpus is small enough that retrieval adds latency/complexity with no precision benefit.

drills.q: Design the enforcement point: a webpage the agent summarizes contains an injected instruction to change a shipping address. Your system prompt already forbids unauthorized address changes. Does the system prompt save you?
drills.a: Only partially and only if enforcement is ALSO implemented outside the model -- a code-level check that the new address matches an allowlisted pattern or requires fresh user confirmation before the tool executes. A system prompt is a strong prior, not a guarantee, for an irreversible action.

drills.q: Constrained decoding guarantees valid JSON syntax. Does it guarantee the agent picked the right tool?
drills.a: No -- constrained decoding constrains the SHAPE of the output, not its correctness. A syntactically perfect tool call with the wrong tool name or hallucinated arguments passes every schema check while being functionally wrong. Syntactic and semantic correctness are two separate checks.

drills.q: You built a 3-agent A2A+FastMCP system. Which two would you merge if redoing it, and what's the test?
drills.a: Merge agents that always run in strict sequence on the same input with no independent retry value (e.g. transcript processing + chunking). Keep separate agents whose failure modes, scaling profiles, or retry semantics genuinely differ (e.g. gap detection, different trigger/cadence). Refusing to name a merge candidate reads as attachment to your own design.

drills.q: Your bounded query-reformulation retry silently drops a constraint (e.g. 'cheap flight to Paris' becomes 'flight to Paris'). How do you catch this class of bug?
drills.a: An eval or invariant check that verifies reformulated queries preserve the original query's key constraints (constraint-extraction compared before/after reformulation, or logging + periodically auditing reformulation diffs) -- don't just trust the rewrite is safe by default.

drills.q: What's the calibration difference for scoring this round vs. the ML/DL round?
drills.a: GenAI is the student's strongest domain, so the bar is calibrated upward -- a HIRE here should be harder to earn than a HIRE on the ML round, and a shallow LEAN HIRE-level pass here is treated as a genuine concern, not an acceptable outcome.
